g1.label: 1. I'm afraid Wednesday afternoon doesn't ___ me: I have a dentist appointment at two.
g1.why: A time suits you when it is convenient; match and agree need other patterns.

g2.label: 2. I can't make Thursday morning. I ___ a presentation in another course at nine; it was fixed weeks ago.
g2.why: A fixed personal arrangement takes the present continuous: I'm giving a presentation.

g3.label: 3. Could we ___ the meeting forward to Tuesday? Friday is too late for the budget.
g3.why: Bring a meeting forward means move it to an earlier time.

g4.label: 4. The room is double-booked, so we'll have to ___ the meeting off until the following week.
g4.why: Put off means postpone; call off means cancel, which does not go with until.

g5.label: 5. Let me just check my ___ and I'll get back to you about Monday.
g5.why: Your diary shows your appointments; an agenda lists meeting points, minutes record them.

g6.label: 6. Does Tuesday at four ___ for everyone, or should we look at Friday?
g6.why: A time works for someone when it is possible for them: does it work for everyone?

g7.label: 7. Nobody has a problem with the afternoon? Shall we ___ four o'clock, then?
g7.why: Shall we say … ? is the fixed phrase for proposing a time.

g8.label: 8. I am writing to ___ our meeting on Tuesday 1 December at 16:00 in Room B2.14.
g8.why: You confirm an arrangement that already exists; assure needs a person as its object.

g9.label: 9. Tuesday is ___ the most convenient time: it only means one shift swap.
g9.why: By far strengthens a superlative: by far the most convenient.

g10.label: 10. I would be grateful ___ you could book a projector for the meeting.
g10.why: The polite request pattern is I would be grateful if you could …
